question: Which of the following correctly classifies the occupational hazard faced by a worker exposed to excessive noise in a textile mill?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Chemical hazards involve exposure to dusts, fumes, gases, or solvents — not noise. Noise is a physical agent.
Correct. Excessive noise is a physical hazard; prolonged exposure causes noise-induced hearing loss (NIHL), a recognised occupational disease.
Biological hazards involve living organisms — bacteria, viruses, or fungi — not physical forces such as noise.
Ergonomic hazards relate to poor workstation design, repetitive strain, or awkward postures — not sound energy.

overallFeedback.feedback: Revisit the hazard classification table. Noise is a physical agent, distinct from chemical, biological, ergonomic, or psychosocial hazards.
Well done. Physical hazards (noise, heat, radiation, vibration) are one of the five occupational hazard categories.
